2012_032_020712regmtg.paragraph: Board agenda and supporting packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of February 7, 2012, held at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. The packet carries the January 17, 2012 organizational and regular meeting minutes, January 27, 2012 retreat minutes, an enrollment projection report prepared by Frederick R. Ignatovich, Ph.D., of STANFRED Consultants, open-enrollment limits for 2012/2013, and band uniform and instrument bid awards. The central action is the 2011-12 budget amendment, which sets the amended General Fund appropriation at $130,078,102 and an amended June 30, 2012 General Fund balance of $21,131,625.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, February 7, 2012, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August.

**Recognition**
Michigan Schools & Government Credit Union mini-grant awards, presented by Bob Vincent, MSGCU Director of Sales and Business Development.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the January 17, 2012 organizational meeting (officers elected through December 31, 2012: Philippart president, Edmunds vice president, Miletti secretary; Mark S. Rajter appointed Treasurer; depository and investment resolution 12-006), the January 17, 2012 regular meeting (104 senior scholar athletes recognized; three Troy High students sharing $50,000 in Siemens Competition scholarship money; TESPA negotiating team named; four Schools of Choice resolutions), and the January 27, 2012 Board retreat, which ran from 6:00 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. at the Administration Building.

**Enrollment projections (Curriculum 7.A)**
Prepared by Frederick R. Ignatovich, Ph.D., STANFRED Consultants. Enrollment history: 2006/2007 12,129; 2007/2008 12,182; 2008/2009 12,165; 2009/2010 12,069; 2010/2011 12,056; 2011/2012 12,328. Five-year outlook 2011-12 to 2016-17:

| Grade level | LOW | MOST LIKELY | HIGH |
|---|---|---|---|
| K-5 | -7.0% | -2.1% | +2.8% |
| 6-8 | +3.0% | +7.4% | +11.8% |
| 9-12 | -6.0% | -0.4% | +5.5% |
| K-12 | -4.3% | +0.7% | +5.8% |

Projected enrollment is calculated by multiplying MOST LIKELY by two, adding HIGH, and dividing by three. Projected totals (excluding roughly 133 SCSE, ECP and GROW students, with the inclusive total in parentheses): 2012/2013 12,244 (12,377); 2013/2014 12,344 (12,477); 2014/2015 12,414 (12,547); 2015/2016 12,446 (12,579); 2016/2017 12,427 (12,560).

**Open enrollment (7.B)**
Athens High School and Troy High School closed to open enrollment for 2012/2013, except not more than 30 incoming ninth graders living in the Troy High attendance area who wish to attend Athens. Applications accepted February 8-24, 2012; siblings of Athens students in grades 9-11 also permitted.

CONSENT AGENDA - ORGANIZATIONAL MEETING MINUTES, JANUARY 17, 2012. President Philippart called the organizational meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building. Present in addition to Ms. Philippart were Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood, along with Superintendent Fowler; administrators Birmingham, Cottone, Jolly, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter, Witt and Wood; and approximately 65 members of the audience. Resolution 12-001 made Ms. Philippart acting chairperson (Ayes 7, Nays 0), and Judy Holmes was appointed temporary secretary. Roll-call votes carried 7-0 elected Ms. Philippart president (12-002), Mrs. Edmunds vice president (12-003), and Mr. Miletti secretary (12-004), each serving until December 31, 2012. Resolution 12-005 appointed Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, as Treasurer of the Troy Board of Education for January through December 2012. Resolution 12-006 adopted the Fund Depositories and Investments resolution for the same period, directing Treasurer Rajter to deposit all public monies, including tax monies, in Bank of America, Bank of New York, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Citizen's Bank, Comerica Bank, Fifth Third Bank, MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus, managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank), PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank, and PNC Bank. Withdrawals may be made by checks bearing the facsimile signature of Treasurer Mark S. Rajter, with the handwritten signature of Rajter or Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler permitted in emergencies on the General Fund and Payroll accounts at Bank of America. PNC Bank accounts established for paying Troy Career Center expenses are drawn on the handwritten signature of the Troy Career Center Manager, Assistant Manager or Program Coordinators. Checks over $10,000 drawn on the Bank of America account for remaining health care claims require the additional handwritten signature of Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent for Human Resources, or Monica Papasian, Finance Director. The Comerica Bank account for health care and dependent care flexible spending claims may be drawn by ACH debit to Next Generation Enrollment, Inc. Funds may be invested according to Board Policy D-1103 and combined across funds under subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code, with authorized institutions Ambassador Capital Management, Bank of America, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Charter One Bank, Citizens Bank, Comerica Bank, Fifth Third Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, MILAF, Morgan Stanley Smith Barney, PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank, and The Private Bank; the certification is signed by Paula Fleming, Secretary, on the 17th day of January 2012. Resolution 12-007 continued designation of the Superintendent of Schools as Deputy Secretary of the Board; 12-008 designated Judy Holmes, Secretary to the Superintendent of Schools, to post notices of meetings; 12-009 adopted the 2012 calendar-year meeting schedule. The organizational meeting adjourned at 7:12 p.m., submitted by Judy Holmes, Acting Secretary, and Todd Miletti, Secretary.

REGULAR BOARD MEETING MINUTES, JANUARY 17, 2012. Called to order at 7:12 p.m. with the same members, administrators and roughly 65 audience members. The Board recognized 104 senior scholar athletes from fall sports who maintained a 3.5 cumulative grade point average while competing, among them Joshua Allen (Football), Arianna Armin (Girls' Swim & Dive), Ujwal Bharath (Boys Tennis), Taylor Bommarito (Volleyball), Sameer Desai (Boys Tennis), Christofer Hatzis (Boys Water Polo), Emma Kollman (Volleyball), Tingxi Liu (Swimming), Marisa Oleski (Girls Golf), Mayara Sanches (Cheerleading), Edgar Wang (Boys Water Polo) and Kevin Zywicki (Boys Tennis). Fall all-state athletes recognized were Zachary Doepke (Boys Soccer), Kelly Feng (Girls Golf), Matthew Kuntzman (Boys Tennis), Jason Leslie (Boys Soccer), Kento Mizusaki (Boys Tennis), Sanath Shettigar (Boys Soccer), Matt Smolinski (Boys Soccer), William Yau (Cross Country) and Richard Zhang (Boys Tennis). Three Troy High School students - seniors Edgar Wang and Justin Yuan and junior Wayne Shu - were recognized as 2011 Siemens Competition winners who will share $50,000 in scholarship money after placing second in early December in a national field of 20 finalists at George Washington University in Washington D.C. For National School Board Recognition month, Ms. Birmingham showed a video, Board members received an original canvas artwork created by Troy art teacher Heather Kelly, and Dr. Machesky and Mrs. Keeling reported a donation made in the Board's honor to the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence. Resolution 12-010 approved the consent agenda: minutes of the December 6, 2011 meeting, minutes of the December 13, 2011 workshop, and the Treasurer's Report for November and December 2011 (7-0). Resolution 12-011 appointed Jasen Witt chief spokesperson with Mark Rajter and Sara Konieczka as team members for negotiations with TESPA/MEA/NEA, whose contract expires June 30, 2012 (7-0). Resolution 12-012 approved new hires Molly Brehm and Erin Hill (7-0). Dr. Machesky presented on OCALP, the Oakland Community Accelerated Learning Program hosted by Oakland Community College, in which Troy was one of five surrounding districts participating. Physical education teacher Jamie Grant presented the new T.R.O.Y. (Teachers Recognizing Outstanding Youth) Fitness Program for grades K-5, replacing the traditional Presidential Physical Fitness Award. Resolutions 12-013 through 12-016, each 7-0, adopted limited Schools of Choice programs for 2012-2013 under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996: nonresident kindergarten and first grade students from within Oakland County, the same from contiguous intermediate school districts, and grades 6-8 at Baker Middle School under both sections. Dr. Fowler gave the third of four updates on the 2011-2012 Superintendent's Goals, addressing Visibility, Facilities Study, Data Processing Cost Analysis, Strategies for Student Success and Community Outreach. Student representative Maggie Steele of Troy High reported on the Gala Concert on Saturday, February 4th and a Snowcoming Dance with Spirit Week; Jonny Dowdall of Athens High reported a student council can drive collecting over 5,000 cans and over 400 pairs of socks, and awards at the University of Michigan Model UN conference in Ann Arbor for Ramis Wadood, Promit Ghosh, Mukund Mohan and Misha Rahman. Ms. Underwood welcomed Karl Schmidt to the Board. Resolution 12-017 moved the Board into closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), by 7-0 roll call; closed session began at 8:37 p.m., the meeting reconvened at 9:28 p.m. and adjourned at 9:29 p.m.

BOARD RETREAT MINUTES, JANUARY 27, 2012. Called to order at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building with all seven members present plus Dr. Fowler, Mrs. Keeling, Dr. Machesky, Mrs. Papasian, Mr. Rajter and Mr. Witt, and one other audience member. Agenda topics: public communication; 2011/2012 First Appropriation Action; 2012/13 - 2014/15 Budget Forecast; 2004 Unexpended Bond Issue Proceeds and Expenditure Recommendations; Custodial and Transportation Contract Renewals; High School Student Feedback from the Board Breakfast; and Board Policy Committee Recommendations. Adjourned at 11:00 p.m.

ENROLLMENT PROJECTIONS (7.A). Analysis provided by Frederick R. Ignatovich, Ph.D., STANFRED Consultants. Enrollment history: 2006/2007 12,129; 2007/2008 12,182; 2008/2009 12,165; 2009/2010 12,069; 2010/2011 12,056; 2011/2012 12,328. Oakland County resident births are charted from 1955 to 2011, sourced from the Michigan Department of Community Health and the National Center for Health Statistics. Birth-to-kindergarten ratios run 5.10 (95-96), 4.69 (96-97), 4.55 (97-98), 4.42 (98-99), 4.58 (99-00), 4.46 (00-01), 4.42 (01-02), 4.58 (02-03), 4.67 (03-04), 4.61 (04-05), 4.65 (05-06), 4.95 (06-07), 5.46 (07-08), 5.27 (08-09), 5.22 (09-10), 5.62 (10-11) and 5.66 (11-12). Kindergarten-to-first-grade cohort ratios run 106.72 (98-99), 106.85 (99-00), 106.97 (00-01), 105.54 (01-02), 106.05 (02-03), 109.70 (03-04), 112.13 (04-05), 105.42 (05-06), 106.88 (06-07), 103.57 (07-08), 101.92 (08-09), 105.54 (09-10), 106.40 (10-11) and 111.80 (11-12). Program history slides record Troy residents attending other public school districts at Fall 2002 - 299, Fall 2006 - 279, Fall 2009 - 395 and Fall 2010 - 432; nonresident students attending Troy at Fall 2002 - 295, Fall 2008 - 450, Fall 2009 - 572 and Fall 2010 - 683 (the same slide also prints Fall 2006 - 320 and Fall 2008 - 326). Troy residents attending charter schools are shown at Fall 2002 - 21, Fall 2006 - 21, Fall 2008 - 25, Fall 2009 - 39, Fall 2010 - 75 and Fall 2011 - 106, with a breakdown of Huron Academy 25, Michigan Virtual Charter Academy 10, Manoogian School 9, Four Corners Montessori Academy 9 and Others 22 (Fall 2007 - 50 also appears). Kindergarten Schools of Choice intake ran Fall 2006 - 31, Fall 2008 - 49, Fall 2009 - 71 and Fall 2010 - 102; first grade SOC intake ran Fall 2006 - 20, Fall 2007 - 12, Fall 2008 - 8, Fall 2009 - 13, Fall 2010 - 28 and Fall 2011 - 35; initial middle school SOC intake for fall 2011 was 25, only at Baker; International Academy-East (IAE) high school SOC freshmen ran Fall 2008 - 30, Fall 2009 - 37, Fall 2010 - 33 and Fall 2011 - 61. Head counts exclude 133 students in ECP (Early Childhood Program), SCSE (Self Contained Special Education) and GROW (post secondary special education). Each projection set gives LOW, MOST LIKELY and HIGH. K-5 head count fell from 5,230 to 4,915 between 1997-98 and 2003-04 (-315 students, -6.0% over six years) and rose from 4,915 to 5,234 between 2003-04 and 2011-12 (+319, +6.5% over eight years); the HIGH projection reaches 5,381 (+147, +2.8%), MOST LIKELY 5,126 (-108, -2.1%) and LOW 4,868 (-366, -7.0%) by 2016-17. Grades 6-8 rose from 2,855 to 2,965 between 1997-98 and 2002-03 (+110, +3.9%) and fell to 2,825 by 2011-12 (-140, -4.7% over nine years); HIGH reaches 3,158 (+333, +11.8%), MOST LIKELY 3,033 (+208, +7.4%) and LOW 2,911 (+86, +3.0%). Grades 9-12 rose from 3,752 to 4,231 between 1997-98 and 2006-07 (+479, +12.8%) and fell to 4,077 by 2011-12 (-154, -3.6%); HIGH reaches 4,303 (+226, +5.5%), MOST LIKELY 4,060 (-17, -0.4%) and LOW 3,833 (-244, -6.0%). K-12 head count was stable from 11,837 in 1997-98 to 11,849 in 2010-11 (+12, +0.1%) before a very substantial increase of +287 students or +2.4% to 12,136 in 2011-12; HIGH reaches 12,842 (+706, +5.8%), MOST LIKELY 12,219 (+83, +0.7%) and LOW 11,612 (-524, -4.3%). Projected future enrollment is calculated by multiplying MOST LIKELY by two, adding HIGH, and dividing by three, yielding by grade band and year: 2012/2013 K-5 5,348, 6-8 2,760, 9-12 4,137, total 12,244 (12,377 including SCSE, ECP and GROW); 2013/2014 5,410 / 2,767 / 4,168, total 12,344 (12,477); 2014/2015 5,408 / 2,800 / 4,207, total 12,414 (12,547); 2015/2016 5,351 / 2,924 / 4,171, total 12,446 (12,579); 2016/2017 5,211 / 3,075 / 4,141, total 12,427 (12,560). The current-enrollment comparison lists 2011/2012 at K-5 5,319, 6-8 2,872, 9-12 4,137 and a total of 12,328 against 2012/2013 projections of 5,348, 2,760, 4,137 and 12,377.

SCHOOLS CLOSED TO OPEN ENROLLMENT (7.B). Administration reviewed elementary, middle and high school attendance areas; Athens and Troy High have been closed to open enrollment for the past three years. The resolution closes both schools for 2012/2013 with the exception of not more than 30 openings for incoming ninth graders who live in the Troy High School attendance area but wish to attend Athens High School; students with siblings attending Athens and currently enrolled in grades 9-11 may also open enroll. OTHER (10). Item 10.A proposes rescheduling the March 6, 2012 Board of Education meeting to March 20, 2012. Item 10.B is the first reading of revisions to Board Policy B-1401, Minutes, and new Board Policy I-1701, Opting Out of Video Presentations, both reviewed by the Board's attorney for compliance with state law, the Open Meetings Act and the Revised School Code. B-1401 requires minutes to record the time, date and place of the meeting, members present and absent, topics discussed and decisions made, the purpose of any closed session, and all roll call votes, resolutions, movers and seconders and vote counts, with roll call votes required for non-unanimous or statutorily required votes; proposed minutes must be available for public inspection within eight business days after a meeting and approved minutes within five business days after approval; records are released under the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, Act No. 442, PA 1976; official minutes are bound and kept in the vault at the administrative office. B-1401 was adopted April 8, 1975 and revised March 15, 1977, January 16, 1979, March 17, 1998 and June 19, 2007. New policy I-1701 states the district may occasionally show video of speeches, presentations and enrichment activities outside the district curriculum that are not produced by the district; parents/guardians wishing to opt out must notify the child's building principal or classroom teacher, will be informed of the right as part of the district's annual notices, and reasonable provisions will be made for students removed from classrooms during video presentations.
